title: AOT code generation — the C pipeline
preamble:
# AOT code generation — the C pipeline

Prefix `IAOT`.

How the reference implementation *produces* AOT code atoms: the
signatures compiled functions expose, the calling convention the
runtime trampoline uses, the pipeline that renders C and invokes a
compiler, the flag model, and the XIP arrangement for ESP32-S3.

## What this is not

Not the AOT capability itself. That the language supports AOT-compiled
rule code, what the `CompiledCode` atom is, how its body is laid out, how a
loader discovers an entry point, and what happens when no blob matches
the architecture — all of that is
[RAOT], and binds
every implementation.

The split exists because the runtime spec must not assume the emission
target is C. An implementation targeting the BEAM would generate
Erlang, pass it to an Erlang compiler, and need an Erlang calling
convention; nothing in the language forbids it. The signatures and
flags here are this implementation's answer, not a contract others must
meet.
